checks.explanation: On June 29, 2023, the Supreme Court struck down affirmative action in college admissions in Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard and the companion UNC case, ruling 6-2/6-3 that race-conscious admissions violated the Equal Protection Clause and Title VI, largely on the strength of evidence that the policies disadvantaged Asian American applicants, exactly as predicted.

sources.title: U.S. Supreme Court Strikes Down Affirmative Action in College Admissions

checks.explanation: Microsoft announced a new multi-year, multibillion-dollar investment in OpenAI on January 23, 2023 (widely reported around $10 billion), extending their partnership and giving Microsoft deep integration with OpenAI's tools, matching the prediction closely.

sources.title: Microsoft announces new multibillion-dollar investment in ChatGPT-maker OpenAI

checks.explanation: Starlink did not go public in 2023, or as a standalone spinoff at all. SpaceX discussed a possible Starlink IPO as early as late 2024 (per November 2023 reporting) but those plans shifted; instead SpaceX itself listed on Nasdaq in June 2026 (raising $75B in the offering, coincidentally the same figure predicted here for Starlink's valuation), with Starlink remaining a subsidiary rather than a separately traded company.

sources.title: SpaceX Weighs Spinning Off Starlink Via IPO as Soon as 2024

checks.explanation: The US did not enter a recession in 2023. Despite widespread recession forecasts at the time (some put the odds near 100%), the economy proved resilient: real GDP grew at a 4.9% annualized rate in Q3 2023, and consumer spending grew steadily (about 2.6% annualized) rather than 'tapping out,' directly contradicting the prediction.

sources.title: As the U.S. Consumer Goes, So Goes the U.S. Economy

checks.explanation: MBS and Xi Jinping agreed in 2023 to deepen energy and trade cooperation, including pricing some Saudi oil sales to China in yuan, and the Bank of China opened its first Riyadh branch in September 2023 to facilitate renminbi settlement, matching the prediction that Saudi Arabia would play a pivotal, influence-building role between major powers.

sources.title: The De-Dollarization of World Economy: Xi-Putin Agreement, Saudi Arabia's Shift to Yuan

checks.explanation: California and San Francisco both faced major 2023 budget crises as predicted: the state deficit reached roughly $68 billion (up from an earlier $32 billion estimate) driven largely by falling tax revenue, while San Francisco closed a budget gap reported between $600 million and $780 million.

sources.title: California descends into budget deficit: 2023 Year in Review

checks.explanation: Relativity Space's Terran 1 launched on March 22, 2023, but failed to reach orbit after an upper-stage malfunction; it did achieve some technical milestones (first methane-fueled rocket to reach space, largely 3D-printed), but the predicted successful launch unlocking a $10 billion order book and SpaceX-like valuation trajectory did not happen. The company later retired the Terran 1 program entirely to focus on the larger Terran R.

sources.title: Relativity's 3D-printed Terran 1 rocket reaches space, but falls short of orbit

checks.explanation: The US became the world's largest LNG exporter in 2023, with exports up 14.7% to 88.9 million metric tons, and Europe (including Turkey) absorbed 66% of that volume, supplying nearly half of all European LNG imports, closely matching the predicted structural dependency and industry win.

sources.title: The United States was the world's largest liquefied natural gas exporter in 2023

checks.explanation: The spread trade's core thesis played out: DeSantis's campaign faded and he dropped out and endorsed Trump just before the New Hampshire primary after a deflating Iowa loss, while Haley outlasted him as Trump's last remaining challenger and continued through the South Carolina primary, matching the predicted long-Haley-short-DeSantis dynamic.

sources.title: Ron DeSantis ends 2024 presidential campaign, endorses Trump over Haley

checks.explanation: Two parts of this compound prediction were correct (Trump was indicted, four times in 2023, and he did win the 2024 nomination), but the most distinctive claim failed completely: there was no pardon-for-not-running deal. Trump ran a full campaign and won the presidency in the November 2024 general election, the opposite of 'agrees to not run.'

sources.title: Trump indicted fourth time, he leads 2024 primary field

checks.explanation: Mixed evidence, not a clean 10-15% Google usage/profitability decline in 2023 specifically. Some informational-search categories saw real erosion (developer Q&A site question volume fell 20-50% post-ChatGPT, academic research referrals down about 32.8%), but Google's overall search traffic and market share stayed roughly stable through the period (about 95% market share maintained, later data showing only a fraction-of-a-percent overall traffic dip through 2025), so the broad usage-loss prediction is only partially borne out.

sources.title: Is SEO Traffic Declining Because of ChatGPT or AI Overviews?

checks.explanation: Capital-intensive growth-stage startups were clearly the biggest business losers of 2023: total VC investment fell 37% year over year, Series B mega-deals ($100M+) dropped from 90 in 2022 to just six in 2023, Series C funding fell 74% year over year in Q1, and down rounds surged from 5.2% to 18.7% of all deals, closely matching the prediction.

sources.title: Down rounds are prevailing as power shifts to VCs again

checks.explanation: Global sovereign debt strain and IMF-related heat materialized largely as predicted: emerging-market public debt-to-GDP hit a record 67% and the IMF issued repeated alarms about worsening sovereign debt dynamics, while the institution faced documented criticism over its uneven, inequitable crisis response across regions.

sources.title: IMF Sounds Alarm on Emerging-Market Debt Crisis

checks.explanation: White-collar 'surplus elite' workers had a rough 2023 as predicted: over 110,000 white-collar professionals were laid off across 400+ tech companies, commentators explicitly described a 'white-collar richcession,' and middle management was specifically targeted as companies looked to cut costs and lean on AI.

sources.title: White-Collar Workers Are Getting the Blues

checks.explanation: Russia and China did deepen ties significantly in 2023, including Xi's March state visit to Moscow and a pledge to increase local-currency trade, but the actual bilateral trade figure was roughly $200 billion (with medium-term projections of $300-350 billion), nowhere near the predicted trillion-dollar scale, an order of magnitude short.

sources.title: 2023 visit by Xi Jinping to Russia

checks.explanation: The dollar's share of global foreign exchange reserves continued eroding through this period, falling to around 58% by 2024 and continuing to multi-decade lows in subsequent years, with central banks diversifying into other currencies and gold, matching the predicted 'beginning of the end' framing (though the shift is gradual, not a sudden collapse).

sources.title: Status of US Dollar as Global Reserve Currency: USD Share Hits 30-Year Low

checks.explanation: The 'laid off tech workers become founders' trend materialized clearly in 2023: a survey of laid-off tech workers found 63% went on to start companies, with over half securing customers or launching within six months, and the phenomenon was widely covered as 'revenge startups' and 'rebounder founders,' matching the prediction's core thesis.

sources.title: Laid-off tech workers launch 'revenge startups' just as money dries up
